HOSTILE INPUT TRACES — more than the required five:
1) First syntactic occurrence skipped by an earlier condition, then later occurrence reached: ready stays 0 until the later lookup; a subsequent scalar failure preserves the result for the next rule, C:317–330,640–647 and T:110–231
2) Helper-returned NULL, followed by negated predicates: pointer=0 plus ready=1 skips retries, the NULL branch yields positive-false before negation, C:620–624,642–647
3) Present zero bitmap: non-NULL pointer remains reusable, each distinct requested bit is false without conflating bitmap contents with readiness, C:620–624,643–647
4) Absent MAC versus present 00:00:00:00:00:00: only mac_present suppresses acquisition; all-zero bytes with presence still query the canonical MAC key, R:232–234, C:664–666 and T:429–475
5) Invalid family 0 or 3: neither IP FD selected, synthetic NULL cached and negation still applies, C:676–690 and T:478–524
6) IPv6 /128 inside overlapping /48 and /0: inherited ancestor bits remain in the retained longest-prefix value, P:381–418 and T:292–359
7) Bits 31/32/63/64/255 and an additional 257th predicate: word/mask boundaries stay within the 32-byte bitmap, compiler/emitter reject overflow rather than truncating policy, P:277–291, C:372–383,620–624 and T:645–738
8) Alternating inputs and removed/restored domain generations: fresh stack state prevents prior-input reuse, unchanged entry-domain presence determines finality, C:297–313 and T:225–289
